title: BISCEPTER: Probability-Driven Bisection for Large-Scale System Software
abstract: arXiv:2610.02995v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Identifying the bug-inducing commit (BIC) is a fundamental step in regression debugging and a key input to emerging BIC-aware fault-localization pipelines. In practice, BICs are commonly obtained with bisection. Standard bisection selects the median commit of the remaining good-bad interval, thereby balancing commit count. This strategy is optimal under the assumption that each commit is equally likely to be the BIC.   This paper shows that this assumption does not match real-world BIC histories. We construct a dataset of 8,172 bug reports from GCC, the Linux kernel, and MariaDB. We find a strong temporal skew: across the studied systems, 50% of BICs lie within the most recent 0.69% of the report-time commit history. Motivated by this observation, we introduce BISCEPTER, a probability-driven bisection approach that uses historical BIC latency as a lightweight prior. translated_title: BISCEPTER：面向大规模系统软件的概率驱动二分法
translated_abstract: 确定引入缺陷的提交（Bug-Inducing Commit, BIC）是回归调试中的一项基础工作，也是新兴的BIC感知故障定位流水线的关键输入。在实践中，BIC通常通过二分法获得。标准二分法选择剩余好-坏区间的中位数提交，从而平衡提交数量。这一策略在“每个提交成为BIC的概率相等”的假设下是最优的。本文表明，这一假设与现实世界中的BIC历史并不相符。我们构建了一个包含来自GCC、Linux内核和MariaDB的8,172份错误报告的数据集。我们发现存在强烈的时间偏斜：在所研究的系统中，50%的BIC位于报告时刻提交历史中最近的0.69%范围内。受这一观察的启发，我们提出了BISCEPTER，一种以历史BIC时延作为轻量级先验的概率驱动二分法方法。它不再选择平均分割剩余提交数量的枢轴点……
tldr: 该论文通过分析8,172份真实错误报告发现引入缺陷的提交存在强烈的时间偏斜（50%的BIC集中在提交历史最近的0.69%内），据此提出BISCEPTER，利用历史BIC时延作为概率先验来指导二分法，突破了传统等概率中位数二分法的局限，从而更高效地定位引入缺陷的提交。
en_tdlr: BISCEPTER is a probability-driven bisection approach that exploits the strong temporal skew of real-world bug-inducing commits—50% of which lie within the most recent 0.69% of the commit history—using historical BIC latency as a lightweight prior to outperform standard median-based bisection.
